topics.topic: Completed-work value when SectionProgress is missing
questions: When planned work exists but no SectionProgress record exists, is completed work value unavailable or exactly zero?
When planned work exists but no progress has ever been recorded, is the section's completed-work value unavailable or exactly zero?

judgement.why: This is the same missing-SectionProgress completed-work question already judged in P5, and its passages were not changed.

precedent.topic: Completed-work value when a section has planned work but no progress record
quotes:
A section without a record has no
recorded progress: its views show `completion_percent = None` and a
completed work value of zero, never an invented 0 %.
precedent.why: M32 distinguishes an absent completion measurement from earned completed-work value and explicitly assigns the latter zero.

topics.topic: Registry base URL startup requirement versus deferred failure
questions: Must a missing or unusable `REGISTRY_BASE_URL` prevent service startup, or may the service start and defer the failure until a Registry operation is attempted?
Must a missing or unusable `REGISTRY_BASE_URL` stop startup, or may the service start and fail only Registry-dependent calls?

judgement.why: This is the same REGISTRY_BASE_URL startup-versus-call-time question already judged in P4, and its passages were not changed.

precedent.topic: Whether invalid Registry base URL configuration blocks startup or causes later transport errors
quotes:
`REGISTRY_BASE_URL` is read by the Registry
gateway at each call, not at start-up: it is no required start-up variable,
and its absence fails only Registry calls (A6).
precedent.why: A30 explicitly permits startup without REGISTRY_BASE_URL and makes its absence fail only a later Registry call.

topics.topic: Accepted and persisted source timestamp representation
questions: Must source timestamps be supplied in UTC, may other offsets be accepted, and are accepted source timestamps persisted as aware values, normalized to naive UTC, or preserved with their original offset?

quotes:
Times a
source supplies — `approved_at`, `published_at` of a snapshot, `confirmed_at`
and `document_date` of a recognition, `photo_date`, `payment_date`, a service
credential's `expires_at` — are
kept as supplied, never replaced by the clock (State 1 Modeling
conventions); their accepted forms and checks, and where in an operation
its one clock read happens, are the accepted spec's, carried to States 6–7.
judgement.why: Accepted timestamp forms, field encodings and persistence serialization are contract/model-closure details owned by State 6, not State 2.

topics.topic: Argon2id parameters and library version
questions: Which exact Argon2id parameters and library version define password and verification-secret hashes?

topics.topic: Audit failure rollback versus unaudited business commit
questions: When the business records can be written but the required audit append fails, must the entire action roll back, or may the business change commit without its audit record?

judgement.why: This is the same audit-append atomicity question already judged in P1, and its passages were not changed.

precedent.topic: Atomicity of significant business mutations when audit persistence fails
quotes:
- **Audit.** A significant success and its audit record commit in one
  transaction through `audit_writer.append_audit` (A13, A23); an idempotent
  replay writes no second creation audit. The audited action, result, reason
  and `entity_id` are the operation's to build.
precedent.why: State 5 requires the business mutation and its audit record to commit in one transaction, so an audit persistence failure prevents the mutation from committing.

topics.topic: Audit requirements for refused catalog actions
questions: Does a refused occurrence of a catalog action count as an action that must write one rejected audit record, or is audit required only for completed actions plus the two named rejected cases?

quotes:
Every other refused operation
rolls its transaction back and writes no record.
judgement.why: A13 explicitly limits rejected audit records to the named snapshot-import and failed-login cases and says every other refused operation writes none.

topics.topic: Authentication versus request-decoding precedence
questions: For a malformed project-scoped request carrying invalid or absent authentication, does decoding fail first, or does the A4 authentication-first sequence apply first?

judgement.why: This is the same request-decoding-versus-authentication precedence question already judged in P7, and its passages were not changed.

precedent.topic: Precedence between authorization failure and request-decoding failure
quotes:
A body that lacks a required field or carries one of the wrong type is
refused by request decoding before the bearer credential is checked: it is
not an import attempt, gets no `import_id` and writes no record.
precedent.why: A7 explicitly makes snapshot request decoding precede bearer authentication; A4 governs the operation after decoding reaches it.

topics.topic: Complete environment-variable contract
questions: What is the complete environment-variable contract, including names, types, requiredness, normalization, defaults and cross-field validation?

quotes:
`config.runtime_environment_variables`: the closed table of environment
  variables, their types, requiredness, normalization and per-environment
  defaults, read into `RuntimeSettings` (R0-10; Factory `a6916180314d`,
  `51d19fdf`).
judgement.why: The complete environment-variable names, types, requiredness, defaults and cross-field schema belong to the State 6 contract/model closure.

topics.topic: Effect of service-principal disablement on existing credentials
questions: Does disabling persistently revoke every ServiceCredential, or only make credentials unusable while the principal remains disabled?

quotes:
`name`, `source_type` and
  `scope_mode` are set at creation and never change; the only modification
  is the status change `active ↔ disabled` (disabling revokes every
  credential of the principal; re-enabling restores none of them, so a
  re-enabled principal needs a newly issued credential).
judgement.why: M13 explicitly says disablement revokes every credential permanently and re-enablement restores none.

topics.topic: Error response for non-EUR expenses
questions: Must a non-EUR expense response expose the typed `currency_mismatch` error, or must it be an undifferentiated empty 422 response?

judgement.why: This is the same externally visible response for a foreign-currency expense already judged in P3, and its passages were not changed.

precedent.topic: Response exposed for a foreign-currency expense
quotes:
- **Refusal.** An operation returns its output or raises one declared
  exception; a refusal is decided before the first write, so it writes
  nothing, except where its Errors say the rejection is itself recorded.
  Exceptions carry data in fields, not messages (A26). The route table maps
  each once to a status with an empty body:
| `BudgetValidationError`, `ExpenseValidationError`, `PhotoValidationError`, `TrackingValidationError`, `FinancialValidationError` | owning module | 422 |
precedent.why: State 5 preserves currency_mismatch as a typed internal financial validation failure while mapping it externally to HTTP 422 with an empty body.

topics.topic: Handling monetary inputs with excess fractional digits
questions: What happens when an input monetary amount has more than two fractional digits?

quotes:
The amount quantized to two digits, ROUND_HALF_UP. An amount with more
fraction digits is rounded, never refused, and the sign rule is applied to
the rounded amount.
judgement.why: The later public operation contract explicitly requires excess fractional digits to be rounded half-up rather than rejected.

topics.topic: New-password Unicode validation and length counting
questions: Exactly which Unicode code points make a new password invalid, and how are the 12–128 code points counted?

quotes:
A new password is 12–128 Unicode code points, contains no NUL/control
  characters, and is hashed exactly as supplied. The portal never trims,
  casefolds, or Unicode-normalizes password plaintext. The exact control
  set is that of the accepted `_validate_new_password`, carried to
  States 6–7.
judgement.divergence: One implementation rejects only NUL and Unicode control characters such as category Cc and accepts U+200E, while another treats Unicode format characters such as U+200E as controls and rejects it; the administrator creating the account observes whether creation succeeds.
judgement.why: The code-point length is decided, but the quoted rule delegates the exact control-character set without stating it, leaving an observable password-refusal condition open.

outcomes: The password is accepted, hashed exactly as supplied, and the pending staff account is created.
The password is rejected as containing a control character, and no staff account is created.
witness.observer: The administrator creating the staff account.
basis:
An administrator creates a staff account with its email, role and an initial
password the administrator chooses and submits in that creation request; the
account is `pending_verification`, and the portal keeps only the password's
hash.

topics.topic: Old credential handling and overlap during rotation
questions: When an administrator rotates a service credential, what happens to the old credential and how is the overlap period bounded?

quotes:
The `PortalStore`, the administrator's `StaffActorContext`, the principal id
and an optional `expires_at`. Any expiry is accepted and stored as
supplied, a past one included, never converted (A28 keeps a supplied time); no expiry means the credential does not expire. A
credential is usable only before its expiry, so one issued with an expiry
already reached is stored but never authenticates.

A12, A17 (a 32-byte secret, the source-fixed A30 entropy of
`create_runtime_app`, issued for the fresh `credential_id`; only the hash
stored); earlier credentials stay valid until revoked; A13
(`principal.credential_issue` naming the new credential as entity, with
its key version).
judgement.why: The later operation contract says issuance leaves earlier credentials valid until explicit revocation and permits the caller to bound overlap with expires_at or leave the credential non-expiring.

topics.topic: Registry failure-category precedence
questions: When one transport exception satisfies more than one category, which RegistryFailureKind wins?

quotes:
Every failed Registry
call is answered with exactly one kind of the table and never with a
fallback; which transport condition counts as which kind, and the order the
gateway tests them in, are the accepted gateway's (notes of
`validate_project_reference`, `get_project_context`,
`list_active_projects`; `rules.registry_failure_translation`), carried to
States 6–7.
judgement.why: The texts do not identify the HTTP client's exception hierarchy or state that any concrete timeout exception also satisfies the transport-error category, so the proposed overlapping-condition history cannot be established from the texts.

topics.topic: Response when an expense-document binary is missing
questions: For an otherwise authorized expense-document record whose binary is missing, must the response be the concealed not-found response, or an explicit storage-unavailable response?

judgement.why: This is the same authorized expense-document missing-content response question already judged in P2, and its passages were not changed.

precedent.topic: Externally visible response for authorized expense-document binary storage or content failures
quotes:
An unknown, cross-project or hidden read is answered the same way, so the caller cannot tell them apart; a refused document read answers that way also when its stored content is missing, oversize or unlisted, while a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as an explicit storage-unavailable error (Factory
`babd5e52`, `rules.binary_delivery_policy`; Factory code
`domain/photo_management.py`; owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour
accepted; technical decisions delegated).
precedent.why: R0-12 specifically requires missing, oversized, or unlisted expense-document content to receive the same concealed answer as an unknown, cross-project, or hidden document.

topics.topic: Snapshot and expense fingerprint specification
questions: What exact fields, type encodings, Unicode treatment, decimal and timestamp normalization, collection ordering, serialization and digest algorithm define each fingerprint?

quotes:
How the
content is canonicalised and digested is the owning function's
(`_canonical_snapshot_fingerprint`, `_canonical_intake_fingerprint`),
carried as it is in the accepted spec to States 6–7 (owner 2026-11-06:
current service behaviour accepted; technical decisions delegated).
judgement.why: Canonical field encoding, serialization, ordering and digest mechanics are owning-function notes and encodings assigned to State 7 rather than State 2.

topics.topic: Staff email syntax and normalization
questions: Which email syntax is accepted, and exactly how is Unicode casefolding applied to the local and domain parts before uniqueness and lookup?

quotes: _normalize_staff_email: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST reject an address containing any whitespace, then syntax-validate and Unicode-casefold it in that order while preserving dots and plus tags and performing no provider-specific rewrite.

_normalize_staff_email: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST require exactly one at-sign, non-empty local and domain components, and at least one dot inside the domain with no empty domain label; therefore a single-label domain such as operator@localhost MUST raise IdentityInputRejected. It MUST also reject whitespace while preserving dots and plus tags.
judgement.why: The later notes define the syntax predicates and require syntax validation followed by Unicode casefolding of the address without provider-specific rewriting.

topics.topic: Viewer visibility of hidden progress-photo metadata
questions: Does client_visible=false exclude a photo from viewer photo listings, or does the viewer still receive its metadata while only the binary is refused?

quotes: list_progress_photos: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST return project-scoped photos only, exclude non-client-visible items for viewer context, and order chronologically by photo_date then photo_id. It MUST project each eligible record onto ProgressPhotoView, so the storage file_ref and the recognition intake_id never leave this module: this function is the only photo list an HTTP route returns, and a storage location in a JSON body would defeat the binary delivery boundary, which hands stored bytes out only through the binary routes.
judgement.why: The later photo-management note explicitly excludes non-client-visible photos from viewer listings.

topics.topic: Viewer-entry rate-limit policy
questions: What rate, time window, burst behavior, memory bound, eviction policy and refusal response apply to viewer entry?

quotes:
The
viewer browser session is the host-only cookie of R0-09; a viewer sign-out
must come from the canonical public origin (viewer entry is not
origin-checked), compared by scheme, host
and effective port, with no pattern matching. The trusted-host, CORS and public-origin
settings and their checks are those of the accepted transport guard
(`rules.http_transport_policy`), carried to States 6–7. Service principals use bearer
headers only.

An entry attempt over the limit is refused before any
code verification and creates no session; the limiter's algorithm, its
bound and its answer are those of the accepted transport guard
(`rules.http_transport_policy.limits.viewer_entry`), with the values of
A30, carried to States 6–7.

Values are knobs; the *existence* of a timeout/TTL/rate limit is an
invariant, its value is config.
judgement.divergence: One implementation's configured attempt limit/window refuses the next valid entry with 429 before verification, while another reasonable limit/window admits it and creates a viewer session; the viewer observes refusal versus successful entry.
judgement.why: A25 makes the threshold and window determine an exact refusal, but points to A30 for values that A30 does not state, leaving two conforming implementations observably different.

witness.initial: An active viewer has a valid non-revoked access credential, and one client network address has made several viewer-entry attempts near a possible window boundary.
events: The viewer submits another entry request from that address using the valid access credential.
outcomes: The configured count/window considers the address over limit, so the transport guard returns 429 before credential verification and creates no session.
The configured count/window considers the attempt admissible, so the credential is verified and a ViewerSession is created.
witness.observer: The viewer attempting to enter the portal.
basis: a successful entry opens a managed `ViewerSession`;

Viewer browser routes accept only that cookie, and
a viewer sign-out is refused unless it comes from the portal's own public
origin (entry is rate limited, not origin-checked; Factory code
`runtime/transport_guard.py` 136–146).

An entry attempt over the limit is refused before any
code verification and creates no session; the limiter's algorithm, its
bound and its answer are those of the accepted transport guard
(`rules.http_transport_policy.limits.viewer_entry`), with the values of
A30, carried to States 6–7.
